summary: This Dockerfile creates an Ubuntu container with curl, ca-certificates, and the yq command-line tool pre-installed. It then bakes a Docker Compose configuration file into the image at /root/demo/compose.yaml that defines a two-service setup (nginx web server and PostgreSQL database), sets up a custom bash prompt to indicate you're in a container, and launches an interactive bash shell when the container starts.

explanations.3: This tells the package installer to skip interactive prompts during installation, so the build doesn't hang waiting for user input.
explanations.5: The && chains commands together so they run in sequence within a single layer; if any command fails, the rest won't execute.
explanations.9: After installing packages, we delete the package manager cache to reduce the final image size since we won't need it again.
explanations.15: TARGETARCH is a special variable that BuildKit automatically sets to either amd64 or arm64 depending on what architecture the image is being built for.
explanations.16: The -fsSL flags make curl fail silently on errors (-f), show no progress bar (-sS), and follow redirects (-L); -o specifies where to save the downloaded file.
explanations.17: The ${TARGETARCH} variable is substituted here so we download the correct yq binary for the current architecture (amd64 or arm64).
explanations.18: chmod +x makes the yq binary executable so it can actually run as a command.
explanations.22: printf with %s\n prints each argument on its own line, which is a reliable way to write multi-line text into a file.
explanations.47: The > operator redirects all the printf output into the compose.yaml file.
explanations.52: The >> appends to .bashrc rather than overwriting it; the PS1 line sets the shell prompt to show a whale emoji and other info to remind users they're in a container.
explanations.54: The -i flag makes bash interactive, so you get a proper shell prompt instead of the container just exiting.
